analysis.title: GS Callahan - GS US TMT quick hits 5 Nov 2026
key_insights: The NDX closed down about 635 bps on the day, roughly 15% off its highs, with semis down 12%+ and nearly 40% off their highs. Both indices had their biggest 1-day drawdown since Mar'20 and are oversold on RSI.

Desk flows were better for sale in Tech/AI with limited signs of defense anywhere. ETFs were about 32% of the tape, their largest share of market volume since June, on a near-record ~27 bn shares traded.
Options volume was the highest in market history, including a record number of puts.
The market's central question is what is priced in for capex (GW) builds over the next few years, more in 2028+ than 2027. There is little investor consensus on 2028+ datacenter builds.

SOX multiples have compressed by about 50% from the June/July highs. The author sees the next debate as whether slowdowns are already over-priced and when the market finds out, since it has not taken comfort from real-time 3Q EPS season feedback.

Sentiment is very tough. Bottoms-up datapoints remain strong (memory pricing, compute pricing, supply/demand visibility, 3Q earnings) while the top-down picture has gotten harder (policy and datacenter construction debates), creating tension in portfolio management.
Top client inbounds were about Semis/AI flows, what is priced in for 2028+, why DASH is down so much, and where a bottom forms. Few clients asked about a shopping list.
A long list of AI and AI-adjacent stocks is now down or flat YTD, including CRDO, AMKR, AVGO, QCOM, NVDA, SNPS, CDNS, PLTR, MDB, AKAM, DT, ZS, COHR, neoclouds and IPPs.

After-hours earnings winners: NET +15% on re-acceleration to +39% y/y, LRCX announced a ~$25bn buyback (~10% of market cap), ABNB +10% on re-acceleration to +16% y/y room night growth, FROG +22% as Cloud revenue accelerated to +60% y/y from +53%.

ABNB said about 40% of customer support issues in Q3 2026 were resolved without a human agent, up from a third in Q2. Support cost per booking fell more than 17% y/y, driven largely by its AI assistant.
October NFPs are due tomorrow morning. GS Economics estimates payrolls +75k, above consensus of +65k and the three-month average of +51k, and average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m in line with consensus.
Charts watched: NDX re-testing its multi-year base trendline, and semis underperforming the market by more than 15 points over 5 days, the worst stretch of underperformance since 2002.

market_movers.rationale: Shares up 15% after earnings as growth re-accelerated to +39% y/y, the best in about 4 years.
Announced a buyback of about $25bn, roughly 10% of market cap.
Shares up 10% on room night growth re-accelerating to +16% y/y.
Shares up 22% as Cloud revenue growth accelerated to +60% y/y from +53% y/y last quarter.

sector_views.rationale: Describes heavy selling, multiples compressed about 50% from the June/July highs and oversold readings. Frames the open question as how much is priced in, without a directional call.

earnings_insights: NET reported after the close on 11/5: shares +15% on revenue growth re-accelerating to +39% y/y, the best growth in about 4 years.
LRCX announced a buyback of about $25bn (about 10% of market cap) alongside earnings on 11/5.
ABNB reported on 11/5: room night growth re-accelerated to +16% y/y and shares rose 10%. Q3 2026 customer support cost per booking fell more than 17% y/y.
FROG reported on 11/5: Cloud revenue growth +60% y/y versus +53% y/y last quarter, shares +22%.
The author says the market has yet to take comfort from real-time feedback during 3Q EPS season, and bottoms-up datapoints including 3Q earnings remain strong.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects a gain above consensus, reflecting a low level of layoffs and a solid signal from big data indicators.
Consensus sits below the GS estimate and above the three-month average.
Baseline against which the October estimates are compared.
In line with consensus, reflecting neutral calendar effects.

risk_factors: Uncertainty over how much datacenter capex (GW) will be built in 2028+ and whether execution issues arise.
Top-down policy and datacenter construction debates are outweighing strong bottoms-up datapoints.
Semis underperformance and the market's failure so far to take comfort from 3Q earnings feedback.

ETFs accounted for about 32% of the tape, their largest share of market volume since June, with elevated 'macro product' volumes especially in Tech and Semis.
Total market volume was near a record at about 27 bn shares.

Desk flows skew to selling in Tech/AI with limited defense and few shopping list conversations.
